context:
Goal: the waiting page saves your answers to git, through a small site on your Cloudflare account.
Problem (rule): the site holds the GitHub token, and anyone who finds its address could call it, so it must know the caller is you; any credential the page keeps goes against the ruling that a token never goes in a page (prose-tending-contract, 11:55 CST), which you doubted at 12:30 CST.
Based on (read): measured 12:35 CST: a claude.ai page cannot call any outside site (its content rules block every outside host), so the page moves off claude.ai and the site serves the page itself, from one address.
Based on (read): Cloudflare's free tier allows 100,000 requests a day and never sleeps (docs read by the site probe).
Departs from: main — adds a site on your Cloudflare account that serves the page and writes your answers to git.

options.gain: No secret in the page; one email code per device.
options.how: A Cloudflare Access gate in front of the site: you log in once per device with a code sent to your email, and the browser keeps the login. Because the site serves the page itself, the login travels with each save.
options.label: Cloudflare login (Recommended)
options.lose: One login step on each new device.

options.gain: Works on any device with no login step.
options.how: Each device keeps a passcode that lets the page write only your answers.
options.label: Device passcode
options.lose: A secret sits in the page, against the no-token-in-page ruling.

options.how: The site accepts any well-formed answer file, with no check on who sent it.
options.label: No credential
options.lose: Anyone with the address could forge an answer.

ref: coordinator 12:34 and 12:38 CST Nov 12, from lane waiting-site-probe
